title: Multi-Member LLC Operating Agreement
summary: A plain-English operating agreement for an LLC with two to four members: ownership, votes, money, exits.
useWhen: Two to four people or companies own an LLC together and need clear rules on control, distributions, transfers and buyouts.
watchOuts: An operating agreement does not form the LLC. You must first file articles (or a certificate) of organization with the state and pay its fees and any annual report or franchise tax.

Keep the LLC separate from your personal finances: its own bank account, signed contracts in the LLC's name, and no mixing of funds. Otherwise a court can 'pierce the veil' and hold members personally liable.
Some states require an operating agreement or have special rules. New York requires a publication step for new LLCs, and California requires a Statement of Information. Verify locally.

Tax classification is a federal choice: single-member LLCs default to disregarded entities and multi-member LLCs default to partnerships. Electing S-corporation or C-corporation treatment requires an IRS filing (Form 2553 or 8832). Talk to a tax adviser.
Bringing in passive investors can make LLC interests 'securities' under federal and state law.

Make sure percentage interests total 100% and match the capital each member contributed, or say why they differ (for example, sweat equity). Granting a profits interest for services has tax consequences.

sections.title: 1. Formation
sections.body: {{llc_name}} (the "Company") is a limited liability company formed under the laws of {{formation_state}} on {{formation_date}}. This operating agreement is effective {{effective_date}}. Principal office: {{principal_office}}.

sections.title: 2. Purpose
sections.body: {{purpose}}

sections.title: 3. Members, contributions and percentages
sections.body:
The members, their initial contributions and percentage interests are:

- **Member A:** {{member_a_name}}, {{member_a_address}}. Contribution: {{member_a_contribution}}. Percentage: {{member_a_percent}}%.
- **Member B:** {{member_b_name}}, {{member_b_address}}. Contribution: {{member_b_contribution}}. Percentage: {{member_b_percent}}%.

sections.title: 4. Member C
sections.body: - **Member C:** {{member_c_name}}, {{member_c_address}}. Contribution: {{member_c_contribution}}. Percentage: {{member_c_percent}}%.

sections.title: 5. Member D
sections.body: - **Member D:** {{member_d_name}}, {{member_d_address}}. Contribution: {{member_d_contribution}}. Percentage: {{member_d_percent}}%.

sections.title: 6. Capital
sections.body: No member must contribute more capital without consenting in writing. If additional capital is approved as a major decision and a member does not contribute their share, the percentages will be adjusted in proportion to total capital contributed. No member earns interest on capital or may withdraw it except as provided here. The Company keeps a capital account for each member under federal tax rules.

sections.title: 7. Management
sections.body: The Company is {{management}}. Ordinary business decisions are made by members holding a majority of percentage interests (or by the manager, if manager-managed).

sections.title: 8. Manager
sections.body: {{manager_name}} is the manager and runs the day-to-day business, subject to the major-decision rules. The manager may be removed or replaced by members holding a majority of percentage interests.

sections.title: 9. Major decisions
10. Distributions and allocations
sections.body: Profits and losses are allocated, and distributions are made, in proportion to percentage interests. Distributions of available cash are made {{distribution_timing}}, after reasonable reserves. No distribution may be made if it would leave the Company insolvent.

sections.title: 11. Tax distributions
sections.body: To the extent cash is available, the Company will distribute to each member, by April 1 of each year, an amount at least equal to the member's allocated share of the Company's taxable income for the prior year multiplied by a reasonable assumed combined tax rate set by majority vote. Tax distributions count as advances against other distributions.

sections.title: 12. Taxes and books
sections.body: The Company will be taxed as a partnership unless the members elect otherwise as a major decision. {{tax_rep}} is the partnership representative for IRS purposes and must keep the members informed. The Company will keep complete books, available to every member on reasonable notice, and provide each member a Schedule K-1 each year.

sections.title: 13. Duties and conflicts
sections.body: Each member will act in good faith and deal fairly with the Company. A member may have other business interests, but may not take a business opportunity that belongs to the Company without first offering it to the Company. Members do not owe duties beyond those in this agreement and non-waivable law.

sections.title: 14. Limited liability and indemnification
sections.body: No member is personally liable for Company debts just because of being a member. The Company will indemnify members and the manager for good-faith acts on its behalf, except for fraud, willful misconduct, knowing violation of law or breach of this agreement. Indemnification is paid only from Company assets.

sections.title: 15. Transfers
sections.body: A member may not sell, give, pledge or otherwise transfer any interest without the written consent of the other members, except to a trust for estate planning where the member keeps control. Before selling to an outsider, a member must first offer the interest to the Company and then to the other members at the same price and terms (right of first refusal). A transferee who is not admitted as a member receives only economic rights.

sections.title: 16. Buyout events
sections.body: If a member dies, becomes permanently disabled, files bankruptcy, divorces and the interest goes to a former spouse, or withdraws, the Company and then the other members have the option, for 90 days, to buy the affected interest. The price is set by {{valuation_method}} as of the event date, payable in cash or over up to {{buyout_months}} months with interest at the applicable federal rate and secured by the purchased interest.

sections.title: 17. Deadlock
sections.body: If members cannot reach a required decision after two good-faith meetings, they will mediate with a mutually acceptable mediator before taking other action.

sections.title: 18. Dissolution
sections.body: The Company dissolves on a major-decision vote or as required by law. On dissolution, the members will wind up the business, pay creditors, then distribute remaining assets according to positive capital account balances.

sections.title: 19. General
sections.body: This agreement is the entire agreement among the members, is governed by the laws of {{formation_state}}, and may be amended only in a writing signed by all members. If any part is unenforceable, the rest remains in effect. Signatures may be electronic and in counterparts.
